## Introduction
This document describes how to secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) Traffic in Contact Center Enterprise (CCE) comprehensive call flow.
## Prerequisites
Certificates generation and import are out of the scope of this document, so certificates for Cisco Unified Communication Manager (CUCM), Customer Voice Portal (CVP) Call Server, Cisco Virtual Voice Browser (CVVB), and Cisco Unified Border Element (CUBE) have to be created and imported to the respective components. If you use self-signed certificates, certificate exchange has to be done among different components.
### Requirements
Cisco recommends that you have knowledge of these topics:
  * CCE
  * CVP
  * CUBE
  * CUCM
  * CVVB


### Components Used
The information in this document is based on Package Contact Center Enterprise (PCCE), CVP, CVVB, and CUCM version 12.6, but it is also applicable to the previous versions.
The information in this document was created from the devices in a specific lab environment. All of the devices used in this document started with a cleared (default) configuration. If your network is live, ensure that you understand the potential impact of any command.
## Configure
**Note** : In the contact center comprehensive call flow, In order to enable secure RTP, secure SIP signals must be enabled. Therefore, configurations in this document enable both secure SIP and SRTP.
The next diagram shows the components engaged in SIP signals and RTP in the contact center comprehensive call flow. When a voice call comes to the system, it first comes via the ingress gateway or CUBE, so start the configurations on CUBE. Next, configure CVP, CVVB, and CUCM.  
  

[![Inbound SIP and RTP Call Flow](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-00.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-00.png "Inbound SIP and RTP Call Flow")
### Task 1: CUBE Secure Configuration
In this task, you configure CUBE to secure SIP protocol messages and RTP.
Required configurations:
  * Configure a Default Trustpoint for the SIP UA
  * Modify the Dial-peers to use TLS and SRTP


Steps:
  1. Open an SSH session to CUBE.


  1. Run these commands to have the SIP stack use the CA certificate of the CUBE. CUBE establishes SIP TLS connection from/to CUCM (198.18.133.3) and CVP (198.18.133.13):


**`Conf t Sip-ua Transport tcp tls v1.2 crypto signaling remote-addr 198.18.133.3 255.255.255.255 trustpoint ms-ca-name crypto signaling remote-addr 198.18.133.13 255.255.255.255 trustpoint ms-ca-name exit`**
[![CUBE SSH Console](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-01.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-01.png "CUBE SSH Console")
  1. Run these commands to enable TLS on the outgoing dial peer to CVP. In this example, dial-peer tag 6000 is used to route calls to CVP:


**`Conf t dial-peer voice 6000 voip session target ipv4:198.18.133.13:5061 session transport tcp tls srtp exit  `**
[![CUBE SSH Console](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-02.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-02.png "CUBE SSH Console")
### Task 2: CVP Secure Configuration
In this task, configure the CVP call server to secure the SIP protocol messages (SIP TLS).
Steps:
  1. Login to the **`UCCE Web Administration`**.
  2. Navigate to **`Call Settings > Route Settings > SIP Server Group`**.  
  



[![SIP Server Group Configuration on CCE Admin Portal](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-03.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-03.png "SIP Server Group Configuration on CCE Admin Portal")
Based on your configurations, you have SIP Server Groups configured for CUCM, CVVB, and CUBE. You need to set secure SIP ports to 5061 for all of them. In this example, these SIP server groups are used:
  * **`cucm1.dcloud.cisco.com`**for CUCM
  * **`vvb1.dcloud.cisco.com`**for CVVB
  * **`cube1.dcloud.cisco.com`** for CUBE


  1. Click **`cucm1.dcloud.cisco.com`**,and then in the**`Members`** tab that shows the details of SIP Server Group Configurations. Set **`SecurePort`**to**`5061`**and click**`Save`**.  
  



[![Setting secure SIP Port for CUCM Server Group](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-04.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-04.png "Setting secure SIP Port for CUCM Server Group")
  1. Click **`vvb1.dcloud.cisco.com`**and then in the**`Members`** tab, set the**`SecurePort`** to **`5061`** and click **`Save`**.  
  



[![Setting secure SIP Port for VVB Server Group](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-05.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-05.png "Setting secure SIP Port for VVB Server Group")
### Task 3: CVVB Secure Configuration
In this task, configure CVVB to secure the SIP protocol messages (SIP TLS) and SRTP.
Steps:
  1. Open the **`Cisco VVB Admin`** page.
  2. Navigate to **`System > System Parameters`**.  
  



[![VVB System Parameters](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-06.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-06.png "VVB System Parameters")
  1. On the **`Security Parameters`**section, choose**`Enable`**for**`TLS (SIP) `**. Keep the**`Supported TLS(SIP) version as TLSv1.2`** and choose **`Enable`**for**`SRTP`**.  
  



[![VVB Security Parameters](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-07.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-07.png "VVB Security Parameters")
  1. Click **`Update`**. Click **`Ok`**when prompted to restart the CVVB engine.  
  



[![Update Security Parameters](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-08.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-08.png "Update Security Parameters")
  1. These changes require a restart of the Cisco VVB engine. In order to restart the VVB engine, navigate to the **`Cisco VVB Serviceability`**, then click**`Go`**.  
  



[![Cisco VVB Serviceability](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-09.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-09.png "Cisco VVB Serviceability")
  1. Navigate to **`Tools > Control Center – Network Services`**.  
  



[![Control Center - Network Services](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-10.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-10.png "Control Center - Network Services")
  1. Choose **`Engine`**and click**`Restart`**.  
  



[![Restarting CVVB Engine Services](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-11.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-11.png "Restarting CVVB Engine Services")
### Task 4: CUCM Secure Configuration
In order to secure SIP messages and RTP on CUCM, perform these configurations:
  * Set CUCM Security Mode to Mixed Mode
  * Configure SIP Trunk Security Profiles for CUBE and CVP
  * Associate SIP Trunk Security Profiles to Respective SIP Trunks and enable SRTP
  * Secure Agents’ device Communication with CUCM


#### **Set CUCM Security Mode to Mixed Mode**
CUCM supports two security modes:
  * Non-secure mode (default mode)
  * Mixed mode (secure mode)


Steps:
  1. Log in to the CUCM administration interface.  
  



[![CUCM Administration Interface](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-12.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-12.png "CUCM Administration Interface")  
  

  1. When you log in to the CUCM, you can navigate to **`System > Enterprise Parameters`**.  
  



[![CUCM Enterprise Parameters](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-13.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-13.png "CUCM Enterprise Parameters")
  1. Under the **`Security Parameters`**section, check if the**`Cluster Security Mode`**is set to**`0`**.  
  



[![CUCM Security Parameters](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-14.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-14.png "CUCM Security Parameters")
  1. If Cluster Security Mode is set to 0, this means cluster security mode is set to non-secure. You need to enable the mixed Mode from CLI.
  2. Open an SSH session to the CUCM.
  3. Upon successful login to CUCM via SSH, run this command:


**utils ctl set-cluster mixed-mode**
  1. Type **`y`**and click**`Enter`**when prompted. This command sets cluster security mode to mixed mode.  
  



[![CUCM SSH Console](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-15.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-15.png "CUCM SSH Console")
  1. For the changes to take effect, restart the **`Cisco CallManager`**and the**`Cisco CTIManager`**services.
  2. In order to restart the services, navigate and log in to**`Cisco Unified Serviceability`**.  
  



[![Cisco Unified Serviceability](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-16.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-16.png "Cisco Unified Serviceability")
  1. After successful login, navigate to **`Tools > Control Center – Feature Services`**.  
  



[![Control Center - Feature Services](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-17.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-17.png "Control Center - Feature Services")  
  

  1. Choose the server and then click **`Go`**.  
  



[![Select Server](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-18.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-18.png "Select Server")
  1. Underneath CM services, choose the **`Cisco CallManager`**, then click**`Restart`** button at the top of the page.  
  



[![Restarting Cisco CallManager Service](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-19.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-19.png "Restarting Cisco CallManager Service")
  1. Confirm the pop-up message and click **`OK`**. Wait for the service to successfully restart.  
  



[![Info Message](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-20.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-20.png "Info Message")
  1. After the successful restart of **`Cisco CallManager`**, choose the**`Cisco CTIManager`** then click **`Restart`**button to restart**`Cisco CTIManager`**service.  
  



[![Restarting Cisco CTI Manager Service](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-21.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-21.png "Restarting Cisco CTI Manager Service")
  1. Confirm the pop-up message and click **`OK`**. Wait for the service to successfully restart.  
  



[![Info Message](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-22.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-22.png "Info Message")
  1. After successful services restart, in order to verify cluster security mode is set to mixed mode, navigate to CUCM administration as explained in Step 5. and then check the **`Cluster Security Mode`**. Now it must be set to**`1`**.  
  



[![Cluster Security Mode is to the Value of '1'](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-23.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-23.png "Cluster Security Mode is to the Value of '1'")
#### Configure SIP Trunk Security Profiles for CUBE and CVP
Steps:
  1. Log in to the CUCM administration interface.
  2. After successful login to CUCM, navigate to **`System > Security > SIP Trunk Security Profile`**in order to create a device security profile for CUBE.  
  



[![CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-24.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-24.png "CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile")
  1. On the top left, click **Add New** to add a new profile.  
  



[![Add a New CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-25.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-25.png "Add a New CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile")  
  

  1. Configure **`SIP Trunk Security Profile`** as this image and then click **`Save`** at the bottom left of the page.  
  



[![Add CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile for CUBE](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-26.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-26.png "Add CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile for CUBE")
5. Ensure to set the **`Secure Certificate Subject or Subject Alternate Name`** to the Common Name (CN) of the CUBE certificate as it must match.
6. Click **`Copy`** button and change the **`Name`**to**`SecureSipTLSforCVP`**. Change**`Secure Certificate Subject`** to the CN of the CVP call server certificate as it must match. Click**`Save`** button.  
  

[![Add CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile for CVP](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-27.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-27.png "Add CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile for CVP")
#### **Associate SIP Trunk Security Profiles to Respective SIP Trunks and Enable SRTP**
Steps:
  1. On the CUCM Administration page, navigate to **`Device > Trunk`**.  
  



[![CUCM Trunk Configuration for CUBE](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-28.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-28.png "CUCM Trunk Configuration for CUBE")
  1. Search for CUBE trunk. In this example, the CUBE trunk name is **`vCube`**, then click**`Find`**.  
  



[![Find SIP Trunks on CUCM for CUBE](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-29.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-29.png "Find SIP Trunks on CUCM for CUBE")
  1. Click **`vCUBE`**to open the vCUBE trunk configuration page.
  2. In **`Device Information`**section, check the**`SRTP Allowed`**check box in order to enable SRTP.  
  



[![Enable SRTP on SIP Trunk Configuration for CUBE](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-30.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-30.png "Enable SRTP on SIP Trunk Configuration for CUBE")
  1. Scroll down to the **`SIP Information`**section, and change the**`Destination Port`**to**`5061`**.
  2. Change **`SIP Trunk Security Profile`**to**`SecureSIPTLSForCube`**.  
  



[![Assign a Security Profile on SIP Trunk Configuration for CUBE](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-31.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-31.png "Assign a Security Profile on SIP Trunk Configuration for CUBE")
  1. Click **`Save`**then**`Rest`**to`save ` and apply changes.  
  



[![Save Configuration](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-32.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-32.png "Save Configuration")
[![Info Message](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-33.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-33.png "Info Message")
  1. Navigate to **`Device > Trunk`**, search for CVP trunk, in this example CVP trunk name is**`cvp-SIP-Trunk`**. Click**`Find`**.  
  



[![Find SIP Trunks on CUCM for CVP](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-34.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-34.png "Find SIP Trunks on CUCM for CVP")
  1. Click **`CVP-SIP-Trunk`**to open the CVP trunk configuration page.
  2. In **`Device Information`**section, check**`SRTP Allowed`**check box in order to enable SRTP.  
  



[![Enable SRTP on SIP Trunk Configuration for CVP](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-35.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-35.png "Enable SRTP on SIP Trunk Configuration for CVP")
  1. Scroll down to the **`SIP Information`**section, change the**`Destination Port`**to**`5061`**.
  2. Change **`SIP Trunk Security Profile`**to**`SecureSIPTLSForCvp`**.  
  



[![Assign a Security Profile on SIP Trunk Configuration for CVP](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-36.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-36.png "Assign a Security Profile on SIP Trunk Configuration for CVP")
  1. Click **`Save`** then **`Rest`**to`save ` and apply changes.  
  



[![Save Configuration Info Message](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-37.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-37.png "Save Configuration Info Message")
#### Secure Agents’ Device Communication with CUCM
In order to enable security features for a device, you must install a Locally Significant Certificate (LSC) and assign the security profile to that device. The LSC possesses the public key for the endpoint, which is signed by the CUCM CAPF private key. It is not installed on phones by default.
  
Steps:
  1. Log in to **`Cisco Unified Serviceability`**interface.
  2. Navigate to **`Tools > Service Activation`**.  
  



[![CUCM Service Activation](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-38.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-38.png "CUCM Service Activation")
  1. Choose the CUCM server and click **`Go`**.  
  



[![Select Server](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-39.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-39.png "Select Server")
  1. Check **`Cisco Certificate Authority Proxy Function`**and click**`Save`**to activate the service. Click**`Ok`**to confirm.  
  



[![Activate Cisco Certificate Authority Proxy Function Service](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-40.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-40.png "Activate Cisco Certificate Authority Proxy Function Service")
  1. Ensure the service is activated then navigate to CUCM administration.  
  



[![CUCM Administration](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-41.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-41.png "CUCM Administration")
  1. After successful login to CUCM administration, navigate to **`System > Security > Phone Security Profile`**in order to create a device security profile for the agent device.  
  



[![Phone Security Profile](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-42.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-42.png "Phone Security Profile")
  1. Find the security profile respective to your agent device type. In this example, a soft phone is used, so choose **`Cisco Unified Client Services Framework - Standard SIP Non-Secure Profile`**. Click copy icon[![Copy Icon](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-43.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-43.png "Copy Icon") in order to copy this profile.  
  



[![Copy Existing Phone Security Profile](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-44.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-44.png "Copy Existing Phone Security Profile")
  1. Rename the profile to **`Cisco Unified Client Services Framework - Secure Profile`**.C hange the parameters as in this image then click **`Save`** at the top left of the page.  
  



[![Add a New Phone Security Profile](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-45.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-45.png "Add a New Phone Security Profile")
  1. After the successful creation of the phone device profile, navigate to **`Device > Phone`**.  
  



[![Phone Configuration](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-46.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-46.png "Phone Configuration")
  1. Click **`Find`**to list all available phones then click agent phone.
  2. Agent phone configuration page opens. Find **`Certification Authority Proxy Function (CAPF) Information`**section. In order to install LSC, set**`Certificate Operation`**to**`Install/Upgrade`**and**`Operation Completes by`**to any future date.  
  



[![Setting CAPF Parameters](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-47.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-47.png "Setting CAPF Parameters")
  1. Find **`Protocol Specific Information`**section and change the**`Device Security Profile`**to**`Cisco Unified Client Services Framework – Secure Profile`**.  
  



[![Assigning Device Security Profile to IP Phone](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-48.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-48.png "Assigning Device Security Profile to IP Phone")
  1. Click **`Save`**at the top left of the page. Ensure the changes are saved successfully, then click**`Reset`**.  
  



[![Save Configuration](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-49.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-49.png "Save Configuration")
  1. A pop-up window opens, click **`Reset`** to confirm the action.  
  



[![Phone Reset](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-50.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-50.png "Phone Reset")
  1. After the agent device registers once again with CUCM, refresh the current page and verify the LSC is installed successfully. Check **`Certification Authority Proxy Function (CAPF) Information`**section,**`Certificate Operation`**must be set to**`No Pending Operation`**and**`Certificate Operation Status`**is set to**`Upgrade Success`****.  
  
**


[![CAPF Information is Updated](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-51.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-51.png "CAPF Information is Updated")
  1. Refer to the same steps from Step. 7 - 13 to secure other agents' devices that you want to use secure SIP and RTP with CUCM.


## Verify
In order to validate RTP is properly secured, perform these steps:
  1. Make a test call to the contact center, and listen to IVR prompt.
  2. At the same time, open the SSH session to vCUBE, and run this command:  
**`show call active voice brief`**  
  



[![show call active voice brief Command Output on CUBE SSH Console](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-52.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-52.png "show call active voice brief Command Output on CUBE SSH Console")
**Tip** : Check if the SRTP is **`on`**between CUBE and VVB (198.18.133.143). If yes, this confirms RTP traffic between CUBE and VVB is secure.
  1. Make an agent available to answer the call.  
.[![Make Agent Ready on Finesse Agent Desktop](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-53.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-53.png "Make Agent Ready on Finesse Agent Desktop")
  2. The agent gets reserved and the call is routed to the agent. Answer the call.
  3. The call gets connected to the agent. Go back to the vCUBE SSH session, and run this command:  
**`show call active voice brief`**  
  



[![show call active voice brief Command Output on CUBE SSH Console](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-54.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-54.png "show call active voice brief Command Output on CUBE SSH Console")
**Tip** : Check if the SRTP is **`on`**between CUBE and the agents' phones (198.18.133.75). If yes, this confirms RTP traffic between CUBE and Agent is secure.
  1. Also, once the call is connected, a security lock is displayed on the agent device. This also confirms the RTP traffic is secure.  
  



[![Secure Lock Appears, Confirm SRTP is Established](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-55.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/220123-configure-secure-rtp-in-contact-center-e-55.png "Secure Lock Appears, Confirm SRTP is Established")
To validate that the SIP signals are properly secured, refer to [Configure Secure SIP Signaling](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac.html "Configure Secure SIP Signaling in Contact Center Enterprise") article.

## Introduction
This document describes how to secure Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) signaling in Contact Center Enterprise (CCE) comprehensive call flow.
## Prerequisites
Certificates generation and import are out of the scope of this document, so certificates for Cisco Unified Communication Manager (CUCM), Customer Voice Portal (CVP) call server, Cisco Virtual Voice Browser (CVVB), and Cisco Unified Border Element (CUBE) have to be created and imported to the respective components. If you use self-signed certificates, certificate exchange has to be done among different components.
### Requirements
Cisco recommends that you have knowledge of these topics:
  * CCE
  * CVP
  * CUBE
  * CUCM
  * CVVB


### Components Used
The information in this document is based on Package Contact Center Enterprise (PCCE), CVP, CVVB, and CUCM version 12.6, but it is also applicable to the earlier versions.
The information in this document was created from the devices in a specific lab environment. All of the devices used in this document started with a cleared (default) configuration. If your network is live, ensure that you understand the potential impact of any command.
## Configure
The next diagram shows the components engaged in SIP signaling in the contact center comprehensive call flow. When a voice call comes to the system, first comes via the ingress gateway or CUBE, so start secure SIP configurations on CUBE. Next, configure CVP, CVVB, and CUCM.
[![Inbound SIP Call Flow](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-00.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-00.png "Inbound SIP Call Flow")
### **Task 1. CUBE Secure Configuration**
In this task, configure CUBE to secure the SIP protocol messages.
Required configurations:
  * Configure a Default Trustpoint for the SIP User Agent (UA)
  * Modify the Dial-peers to use Transport Layer Security (TLS)


Steps:
  1. Open Secure Shell (SSH) session to CUBE.
  2. Run these commands to have the SIP stack use the Certificate Authority (CA) certificate of the CUBE. CUBE establishes a SIP TLS connection from/to CUCM (198.18.133.3) and CVP (198.18.133.13).


**`conf t sip-ua transport tcp tls v1.2 crypto signaling remote-addr 198.18.133.3 255.255.255.255 trustpoint ms-ca-name crypto signaling remote-addr 198.18.133.13 255.255.255.255 trustpoint ms-ca-name exit`**
[![CUBE SSH Console](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-01.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-01.png "CUBE SSH Console")
  1. Run these commands to enable TLS on the outgoing dial peer to CVP. In this example, dial-peer tag 6000 is used to route calls to CVP.


**`Conf t dial-peer voice 6000 voip session target ipv4:198.18.133.13:5061 session transport tcp tls exit  `**
[![CUBE SSH Console](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-02.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-02.png "CUBE SSH Console")
### **Task 2. CVP Secure Configuration**
In this task, configure the CVP call server to secure the SIP protocol messages (SIP TLS).
Steps:
  1. Log in to**`UCCE Web Administration`**.
  2. Navigate to **`Call Settings > Route Settings > SIP Server Group`**`.`  



[![SIP Server Group Configuration on CCE Admin Portal](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-03.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-03.png "SIP Server Group Configuration on CCE Admin Portal")
  
Based on your configurations, you have SIP Server Groups configured for CUCM, CVVB, and CUBE. You need to set secure SIP ports to 5061 for all of them. In this example, these SIP server groups are used:
  * **`cucm1.dcloud.cisco.com`**for CUCM
  * **`vvb1.dcloud.cisco.com`**for CVVB
  * **`cube1.dcloud.cisco.com`** for CUBE


  1. Click **`cucm1.dcloud.cisco.com`** and then in the**`Members` **tab, which shows the details of the SIP Server Group Configuration. Set **`SecurePort`**to**`5061`**and click**`Save`.  
  
**


[![Setting Secure SIP Port for CUCM Server Group](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-04.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-04.png "Setting Secure SIP Port for CUCM Server Group")
  1. Click **`vvb1.dcloud.cisco.com`**and then in the**`Members` **tab. Set SecurePort to **`5061`**and click**`Save`**.  
  



[![Setting Secure SIP Port for VVB Server Group](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-05.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-05.png "Setting Secure SIP Port for VVB Server Group")
### **Task 3. CVVB Secure Configuration**
In this task, configure CVVB to secure the SIP protocol messages (SIP TLS).
Steps:
  1. Log in to`**  `Cisco VVB Administration`**` page.
  2. Navigate to **`System > System Parameters`**.  
  



[![VVB System Parameters](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-06.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-06.png "VVB System Parameters")
  1. In the **`Security Parameters`**section, choose**`Enable`**for**`TLS(SIP)`.** Keep **`Supported TLS(SIP) version`** as **`TLSv1.2`**.  
  



[![VVB Security Parameters](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-07.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-07.png "VVB Security Parameters")
  1. Click ****Update****. Click **`Ok`**when prompted to restart CVVB engine.  
  



[![Update Security Parameters](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-08.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-08.png "Update Security Parameters")  
  

  1. These changes require a restart of the Cisco VVB engine. In order to restart the VVB engine, navigate to **`Cisco VVB Serviceability`**then click**`Go`**.  
  



[![Cisco VVB Serviceability](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-09.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-09.png "Cisco VVB Serviceability")
  1. Navigate to **`Tools > Control Center – Network Services`**`.  
`


[![Control Center - Network Services](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-10.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-10.png "Control Center - Network Services")
  1. Choose **`Engine`**and click**`Restart`**.  
  



[![Control Center - Network Services](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-11.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-11.png "Control Center - Network Services")
### **Task 4. CUCM Secure Configuration**
In order to secure SIP messages on CUCM, perform the next configurations:
  * Set CUCM Security Mode to Mixed Mode
  * Configure SIP Trunk Security Profiles for CUBE and CVP
  * Associate SIP Trunk Security Profiles to Respective SIP Trunks
  * Secure Agents’ Device Communication with CUCM


#### **Set CUCM Security Mode to Mixed Mode**
CUCM supports two security modes:
  * Non-secure mode (default mode)
  * Mixed mode (secure mode)


Steps:
  1. In order to set the security mode to Mixed Mode, log in to **`Cisco Unified CM Administration`** interface.  
  



[![CUCM Administration Interface](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-12.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-12.png "CUCM Administration Interface")
  1. After you have successfully logged in to CUCM, navigate to **`System > Enterprise Parameters`**.  
  



[![CUCM Enterprise Parameters](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-13.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-13.png "CUCM Enterprise Parameters")
  1. Underneath the `**`Security Parameters`**`Section, check if**`Cluster Security Mode`**is set to**`0`**.  
  



[![CUCM Security Parameters](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-14.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-14.png "CUCM Security Parameters")  
  

  1. If Cluster Security Mode is set as 0, this means cluster security mode is set to non-secure. You need to enable the mixed Mode from CLI.
  2. Open an SSH session to the CUCM.
  3. After you have successfully logged to CUCM via SSH, run this command: **`utils ctl set-cluster mixed-mode`**


  1. Type **`y`**and click****Enter**** when prompted. This command sets cluster security mode to mixed mode.  
  



[![CUCM SSH Console](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-15.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-15.png "CUCM SSH Console")  
  

  1. For the changes to take effect, restart **`Cisco CallManager`** and **`Cisco CTIManager`** services.
  2. In order to restart the services, navigate and log in to **``Cisco Unified Serviceability``**.  
  



[![Cisco Unified Serviceability](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-16.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-16.png "Cisco Unified Serviceability")
  1. After you have successfully logged in, navigate to **`Tools > Control Center – Feature Services`**.  
  



[![Control Center - Feature Services](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-17.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-17.png "Control Center - Feature Services")
  1. Choose the server then click **`Go`**.  
  



[![Select Server](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-18.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-18.png "Select Server")  
  

  1. Underneath the CM services, choose `**`Cisco CallManager`**` then click **`Restart`** button on top of the page.  
  



[![Restarting Cisco Call Manager Services](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-19.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-19.png "Restarting Cisco Call Manager Services")
  1. Confirm the pop-up message and click **`OK`**. Wait for the service to successfully restart.  
  



[![Info Message](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-20.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-20.png "Info Message")
  1. After a successful restart of **`Cisco CallManager`**, choose Cisco**`CTIManager` **then click **`Restart`**button to restart**`Cisco CTIManager`** service.  
  



[![Restarting Cisco CTI Manager Service](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-21.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-21.png "Restarting Cisco CTI Manager Service")
  1. Confirm the pop-up message and click **`OK`**. Wait for the service to successfully restart.  
  



[![Info Message](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-22.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-22.png "Info Message")
  1. After services successfully restart, verify cluster security mode is set to mixed mode, navigate to CUCM administration as explained in Step 5. then check the **`Cluster Security Mode`**. Now it must be set to **`1`**.  
  



[![Cluster Security Mode is to the Value of '1'](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-23.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-23.png "Cluster Security Mode is to the Value of '1'")
#### Configure SIP Trunk Security Profiles for CUBE and CVP
Steps:
  1. Log in to **`CUCM administration`** interface.
  2. After successful login to CUCM, navigate to `**`System > Security > SIP Trunk Security Profile`**` in order to create a device security profile for CUBE.  
  



[![CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-24.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-24.png "CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile")
  1. On the top left, click **`Add New`** in order to add a new profile.  
  



[![Add New CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-25.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-25.png "Add New CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile")  
  

  1. Configure **`SIP Trunk Security Profile`**as shown in this image then click**`Save`** at the bottom left of the page to **`Save`** it.  
  



[![Add CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile for CUBE](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-26.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-26.png "Add CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile for CUBE")
5. Ensure to set the **`Secure Certificate Subject or Subject Alternate Name`** to the Common Name (CN) of the CUBE certificate as it must match.
6. Click **`Copy`** button and change the **`Name`**to**`SecureSipTLSforCVP`**and the`Secure Certificate Subject ` to the CN of the CVP call server certificate as it must match. Click **``Save``**button.  
  

[![Add CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile for CVP](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-27.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-27.png "Add CUCM SIP Trunk Security Profile for CVP")
#### Associate SIP Trunk Security Profiles to Respective SIP Trunks
Steps:
  1. On the CUCM Administration page, navigate to **`Device > Trunk`**.  
  



[![CUCM Trunk Configuration for CUBE](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-28.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-28.png "CUCM Trunk Configuration for CUBE")
  1. Search for CUBE trunk. In this example, the CUBE trunk name is **`vCube`.** Click **`Find`**.  
  



[![Find SIP Trunks on CUCM for CUBE](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-29.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-29.png "Find SIP Trunks on CUCM for CUBE")
  1. Click vCUBE to open the vCUBE trunk configuration page.
  2. Scroll down to **`SIP Information`**section, and change the**`Destination Port`** to **`5061`**.
  3. Change **`SIP Trunk Security Profile`**to**`SecureSIPTLSForCube`**.  
  



[![SIP Trunk Configuration for CUBE](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-30.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-30.png "SIP Trunk Configuration for CUBE")
  1. Click **``Save``**then**`Rest`**in order to**`Save`**and apply changes.  
  



[![Save Configuration](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-31.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-31.png "Save Configuration")
  
[![Info Message](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-32.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-32.png "Info Message")
  1. Navigate to **`Device > Trunk`**, and search for CVP trunk. In this example, the CVP trunk name is**`cvp-SIP-Trunk`.** Click **`Find`**.  
  



[![CUCM Trunk Configuration for CVP](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-33.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-33.png "CUCM Trunk Configuration for CVP")
  1. Click **`CVP-SIP-Trunk`**in order to open the CVP trunk configuration page.
  2. Scroll down to **`SIP Information`**section, and change**`Destination Port`** to **`5061`.**
  3. Change **`SIP Trunk Security Profile`** to **`SecureSIPTLSForCvp`**.  
  



[![Find SIP Trunks on CUCM for CVP](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-34.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-34.png "Find SIP Trunks on CUCM for CVP")
  1. Click **`Save`**then**`Rest`**in order to`save` and apply changes.  
  



[![SIP Trunk Configuration for CVP](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-35.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-35.png "SIP Trunk Configuration for CVP")  
  

[![Save Configuration](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-36.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-36.png "Save Configuration")
#### **Secure Agents’ Device Communication with CUCM**
In order to enable security features for a device, you must install a Locally Significant Certificate (LSC) and assign a security profile to that device. The LSC possesses the public key for the endpoint, which is signed by the Certificate Authority Proxy Function (CAPF) private key. It is not installed on phones by default.
Steps:
  1. Log in to **`Cisco Unified Serviceability Interface`**.
  2. Navigate to **`Tools > Service Activation`****.  
  
**


[![Info Message](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-37.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-37.png "Info Message")
  1. Choose the CUCM server and Click **`Go`.  
  
**


[![CUCM Service Activation](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-38.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-38.png "CUCM Service Activation")
  1. Check **`Cisco Certificate Authority Proxy Function`**and click**`Save`**to activate the service. Click**`Ok`**to confirm.  
  



[![Select Server](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-39.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-39.png "Select Server")
  1. Ensure the service is activated then navigate to **`Cisco Unified CM Administration`**.  
  



[![Activate Cisco Certificate Authority Proxy Function Service](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-40.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-40.png "Activate Cisco Certificate Authority Proxy Function Service")
  1. After you have successfully logged in to CUCM administration, navigate to **`System > Security > Phone Security Profile`** in order to create a device security profile for the agent device.  
  



[![CUCM Administration](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-41.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-41.png "CUCM Administration")
  1. Find the security profiles respective to your agent device type. In this example, a soft phone is used, so choose **`Cisco Unified Client Services Framework - Standard SIP Non-Secure Profile`.** Click **`Copy`**[![Phone Security Profile](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-42.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-42.png "Phone Security Profile")in order to copy this profile.  
  



[![Copy Existing Phone Security Profile](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-43.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-43.png "Copy Existing Phone Security Profile")
  1. Rename the profile to **`Cisco Unified Client Services Framework - Secure Profile`**,change the parameters as shown in this image, then click**`Save`**at the top left of the page.  
  



[![Add New Phone Security Profile](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-44.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-44.png "Add New Phone Security Profile")
  1. After the successful creation of the phone device profile, navigate to **`Device > Phone`**.**  
  
**


[![Phone Configuration](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-45.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-45.png "Phone Configuration")
  1. Click **`Find`**in order to list all available phones, then click agent phone.
  2. Agent phone configuration page opens. Find **`Certification Authority Proxy Function (CAPF) Information`**section. In order to install LSC, set**`Certificate Operation`**to**`Install/Upgrade`**and**`Operation Completes by`**to any future date.  
  



[![Setting CAPF Parameters](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-46.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-46.png "Setting CAPF Parameters")
  1. Find **`Protocol Specific Information`**section. Change**`Device Security Profile`**to**`Cisco Unified Client Services Framework – Secure Profile`**.  
  



[![Assigning Device Security Profile to IP Phone](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-47.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-47.png "Assigning Device Security Profile to IP Phone")
  1. Click **`Save`**at the top left of the page. Ensure the changes are saved successfully and click**`Reset`**.  
  



[![Save Configuration](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-48.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-48.png "Save Configuration")
  1. A pop-up window opens, click **`Reset`** to confirm the action.  
  



[![Phone Reset](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-49.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-49.png "Phone Reset")
  1. After the agent device registers once again with CUCM, refresh the current page and verify the LSC is installed successfully. Check **`Certification Authority Proxy Function (CAPF) Information`**section,**`Certificate Operation`**must be set to**`No Pending Operation`**, and**`Certificate Operation Status`**is set to**`Upgrade Success`**.  
  



[![CAPF Information is Updated](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-50.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-50.png "CAPF Information is Updated")
  1. Refer Steps. 7-13 in order to secure other agents devices that you want to use to secure SIP with CUCM.


## Verify
In order to validate SIP signaling is properly secured, perform these steps:
  1. Open SSH session to vCUBE, run the command **`show sip-ua connections tcp tls detail`**, and confirm that there is no TLS connection established at the moment with CVP (198.18.133.13).  
  



[![show sip-ua connections tcp tls detail Output on CUBE SSH Console](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-51.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-51.png "show sip-ua connections tcp tls detail Output on CUBE SSH Console")  
  

**Note** : At this moment, only one active TLS session with CUCM, for SIP Options is enabled on CUCM (198.18.133.3). If no SIP Options are enabled, no SIP TLS connection exists.
  1. Log in to CVP and start Wireshark.
  2. Make a test call to contact center number.
  3. Navigate to the CVP session; on Wireshark, run this filter in order to check SIP signaling with CUBE:  
`**ip.addr == 198.18.133.226 && tls && tcp.port==5061**`  
  



[![Packet Capture Filtering CVP Secure SIP Signals Between CVP and CUBE](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-52.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-52.png "Packet Capture Filtering CVP Secure SIP Signals Between CVP and CUBE")
**Check** : Is SIP over TLS connection established? If yes, the output confirms SIP signals between CVP and CUBE are secured.
5. Check the SIP TLS connection between CVP and CVVB. In the same Wireshark session, run this filter:
**`ip.addr == 198.18.133.143 && tls && tcp.port==5061`  
  
**
[![Packet Capture Filtering CVP Secure SIP Signals Between CVP and VVB](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-53.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-53.png "Packet Capture Filtering CVP Secure SIP Signals Between CVP and VVB")
**Check** : Is SIP over TLS connection established? If yes, the output confirms SIP signals between CVP and CVVB are secured.
6. You can also verify the SIP TLS connection with CVP from CUBE. Navigate to the vCUBE SSH session, and run this command to check secure sip signals:  
**`show sip-ua connections tcp tls detail`**  
  
  

[![SIP TLS Connection Between CVP and CUBE from CUBE SSH Console](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-54.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-54.png "SIP TLS Connection Between CVP and CUBE from CUBE SSH Console")
**Check** : Is SIP over TLS connection established with CVP? If yes, the output confirms SIP signals between CVP and CUBE are secured.
7. At this moment, the call is active and you hear Music on Hold (MOH) as there is no agent available to answer the call.
8. Make the agent available to answer the call.  
  

.[![Make Agent Ready on Finesse Agent Desktop](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-55.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-55.png "Make Agent Ready on Finesse Agent Desktop")
9. Agent gets reserved and the call is routed to him/her. Click **`Answer`**to answer the call.  
  

[![Answer Incoming Call on Finesse Desktop](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-56.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-56.png "Answer Incoming Call on Finesse Desktop")
  
10. Call connects to the agent.
11. In order to verify SIP signals between CVP and CUCM, navigate to the CVP session, and run this filter in Wireshark:  
**`ip.addr == 198.18.133.3 && tls && tcp.port==5061`**  
  

[![Packet Capture Filtering Secure SIP Signals between CVP and CUCM](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-57.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/contact-center/unified-contact-center-enterprise/218434-configure-secure-sip-signaling-in-contac-57.png "Packet Capture Filtering Secure SIP Signals between CVP and CUCM")
**Check** : Are all SIP communications with CUCM (198.18.133.3) over TLS? If yes, the output confirms SIP signals between CVP and CUCM are secured.
## Troubleshoot
If TLS is not established, run these commands on CUBE to enable debug TLS to troubleshoot:
  * **`Debug ssl openssl errors`**
  * **`Debug ssl openssl msg`**
  * **`Debug ssl openssl states`**
